message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Standard atomic weight** | 1.008 u (average of isotopes) |
| **Isotopes** | ¹H (protium, 99.98 %), ²H (deuterium, 0.02 %), ³H (tritium, trace) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Electron affinity** | –72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ (negative, meaning energy is released when H gains an electron) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.9 °C (20.4 K) |
| **Melting point** | –259.2 °C (14.0 K) |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈0.00008988 kg m⁻³) |
| **Molar volume at STP** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| **State at room temperature** | Gas (colorless, odorless, non‑metallic) |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; forms covalent bonds with most elements; reacts with oxygen to form water (combustion). |
| **Acidity/Basicity** | Acts as a weak acid (hydrogen ion donor) in aqueous solutions; forms hydronium (H₃O⁺). |
| **Bonding** | Forms diatomic molecules (H₂) via single covalent bond; can form hydrogen bonds (weak dipole–dipole interactions) in compounds like water. |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman, Balmer, Paschen series in UV/visible/IR spectra. |
| **Magnetic properties** | Diamagnetic (no unpaired electrons). |
| **Electrical conductivity** | Poor conductor in gaseous state; becomes metallic under extreme pressure (~400 GPa). |
| **Thermal conductivity** | High (≈0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 300 K). |
| **Specific heat capacity (gas)** | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (at constant pressure). |
| **Solubility in water** | ~0.0006 mol L⁻¹ at 25 °C (very low). |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; explosive mixtures with air (4–75 % H₂). |
| **Applications** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), rocket propellant, industrial hydrogenation, laboratory standard gas, medical imaging (MRI contrast agents). |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element** – only one proton and one electron (except for deuterium/tritium).
- **Highly reactive** – readily forms bonds, especially with oxygen (water) and metals (forming hydrides).
- **Low density & high diffusivity** – makes it useful as a clean energy carrier.
- **Unique spectral fingerprints** – key in astrophysics and spectroscopy.
- **Under extreme conditions** – can become metallic, exhibiting superconductivity at very low temperatures.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or its implications!
